Answer: A
Reason: Following a pneumothorax and subsequent lung reexpansion, the pleural layers of the azygos fissure often become thickened or separated by fluid/inflammation, making the fissure appear more prominent on chest X-ray (Figure 3a) compared to the baseline appearance. The teardrop opacity (azygos vein) typically remains visible, ruling out options suggesting its absence or total resorption of the fissure.
